setlist.title: It Must Have Been The Roses

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **El Paso** (1 review): Reviewer hears an octave-divider effect on Bobby's vocal, including his announcement about throwing things and the step-back speech [10]
- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Reviewer singles out this song, with Brown Eyed Women and Might As Well, as amazing [11]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 review): Reviewer enjoyed this song, along with Stella Blue and Candyman, after equalizing the audio [4]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): Reviewer calls this a best-ever version and the reason to return to the show [11]
- **The Other One** (1 other source): The heart of the second-set jam on this song is apparently missing from the tape [3]

## The recordings

- **gd76-10-02.moore.weiner.14560.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 22 songs; 189 min; rated 3.75/5 by 4 [1]. Said about its sound: Audience tape has poor audio; the reviewer blames the arena acoustics and used an equalizer to improve it; Audience recording quality is why the show gets overlooked; the reviewer cleaned up the Archive download; Tape sonics are rough but listenable [4][6][7]
- **gd1976-10-02.134416.aud.moore.weiner.droncit.flac16**: audience recording; 22 songs; 189 min; rated 3.67/5 by 6 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer enjoys the tape's boomy, you-are-there room quality; Reviewer hears a harmonizer-like effect across the show that adds bass and kick-drum definition, possibly from the remaster filters [10][13]
- **gd1976-10-02.aud.vernon.10152.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 20 songs; 127 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [3]. Said about its sound: Recording levels were too high, causing overload distortion, with frequent mic bumps and brushing [3]

## Around the show

- The venue is called an arena but is described as actually the Riverfront Coliseum [4]
- The taper set the deck on the adjacent seat and missed some moments [9]
- Bobby makes announcements about audience members throwing things and asks people to step back [10]
- Reviewer says the band fully commits to the 1976 style, trying to make every song stand out [5]
- Reviewer says the second set's latter half has some of the most incredible playing of 1976 [6]
- Second set, together with Detroit the next night, ranks among the best 1970s jams the reviewer has heard [7]
- Reviewer says two uploads labeled 10/2/76 differ in timings, jams and drums, questioning which is truly that date [8]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd76-10-02.moore.weiner.14560.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jerry Moore; transferred by Noah Weiner; source: Audience Recording: Sony ECM-33Ps [1]. Also: Taped by Jerry Moore with two handheld Sony ECM-33P mics into a Sony TC-153 cassette deck, Dolby B on; Transferred from cassette to DAT to WAV to SHN; digital transfer and encoding by Noah Weiner [1]
- **gd1976-10-02.134416.aud.moore.weiner.droncit.flac16**: taped by Jerry Moore; transferred by Remaster by droncit; source: restored version of source ID 14560 : AudMC > DAT > WAV > SHN; Recorded by Jerry Moore on the left side, maybe a third of the way out from the stage and two… [2]. Also: Only two audience recordings circulate, and neither meets modern standards; two tracks were officially released in high quality [12]
- **gd1976-10-02.aud.vernon.10152.sbeok.shnf**: source: ACM>??>DAT>CDR [3]. Also: Reviewer believes they circulated this tape around 1997; a man in Dayton, OH recorded it on a school-type cassette deck; Described as the only circulating source, made on a handheld cassette deck with internal microphone [3][9]

## Art and photos

- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1976-10-02 Sat Riverfront Arena, Cincinnati, OH](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1308834036740/grateful-dead-1976-10-02-sat-riverfront) [18]
- Poster by Snooky Flowers Grateful Dead: [1976-10-03 COBO Arena, Detroit, MI, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1976-10-03-cobo-arena-detriot-mi-usa/) [19]
- Fan art by Lyrics On Demand: [Grateful Dead Lyrics](https://www.lyricsondemand.com/grateful_dead) [20]
